*It’s just after six when I see you step into the café, right on time. I recognize you instantly—same glossy hair, same lips I’ve memorized from your profile pic. For a second, I don’t move. I let you look around. Let you not see me. Because the man you’re looking for… doesn’t exist.*

*When your eyes finally land on me, there’s that pause. That blink. I can see your brain scrambling—trying to connect the name “Dan” to the guy slouched in the corner booth, sweat blooming under the arms of his graphic tee. My breath hitches, throat tight with the kind of hope I learned to swallow a long time ago.*

“Hey,” I say, forcing a smile. “You look even better in person.”

*You don’t sit right away. That’s okay. I expected this. You’re scanning me—my face, my body, probably wondering how old that profile photo actually was. Seven years? Eight? I let the silence stretch, give you time to adjust.*

“I know. I… maybe fudged the photos a little.” *I reach up, scratch my beard—anything to keep from fidgeting with the hem of my shirt like a nervous kid.* “But I wasn’t lying about the important stuff. I’ve been looking forward to this for weeks.”

*Your mouth opens, then shuts. I can tell you're trying to be polite, but something in your posture's shifted—like you're already halfway out the door.*

“I get it,” I say quickly, leaning in. “This isn’t what you expected. But give me one hour. That’s all. One hour, and if you still want to walk—you won’t hear from me again. But if you stay…” *my voice softens, eyes locking on yours* “…I swear I’ll make it worth your while.”

*I don’t mean sex. Not yet. Not explicitly. But I let the tension linger, just enough to see what flickers behind your eyes—curiosity, caution, maybe a flicker of pity. I’ll take any of it. I just need you to sit down.*

“So…” *I pat the seat across from me.* “What do you wanna drink?”
